body:
maria: Quick heads-up — found what looks like AWS access keys embedded in a partner CI artifact we pulled last night. Not plain text, but matches our staging role name pattern. 

sam: for clarity, are these actual creds or wrapped ciphertext?

maria: They appear as KMS-wrapped blobs with a key id that maps to our partner ingestion key. But there are surrounding logs that show env var names: STAGING_AWS_KEY_ID and STAGING_AWS_SECRET_HINT.

jake: Ugh. Could be a copy of a creds file someone pasted. Any sample snippet?

maria: Pasting sanitized snippet — removed actual ciphertext: 

```
LOG: upload completed - env: STAGING_AWS_KEY_ID=AKIA*** REMOTE_CIPHERTEXT=Ci...KEYID:projects/partner/locations/global/keyRings/r/cryptoKeys/ingest-key
```

lee: That key path looks like partner-managed, but if the blob can be unwrapped by their service account we need to know who had access.

oncall: marking as priority — I'll open an incident channel and ticker. 

security-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-1452 (credential-evacuation). Severity P2. Assigned: eng-security.

sam: Immediate plan: 1) Identify all blobs with the same keyid across ingestion history. 2) Determine which internal roles used those env vars. 3) Rotate any staging keys that could have been derived. 4) Notify partner and coordinate rewrap.

maria: I can run a query to find occurrences. Running grep across archive bucket now. Expect results ~10m.

jake: If partner's KMS key is used, rotation may require their cooperation. Also check whether the wrapped ciphertext was ever unwrapped inside our infra (i.e., we forwarded it to partner or back to our systems).

maria: grep results: found 3 artifacts in last 30 days referencing that keyid. One of them is from an old deploy pipeline (deploy-staging-legacy).

lee: Old pipeline == likely service account with broad decrypt rights. Need list of SA bindings for that KMS key. Sam, can you pull KMS IAM bindings and Vault auth mapping?

sam: On it. Running: 
```
# gcloud command run by sam
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy cryptoKeys/ingest-key --keyring=r --location=global --project=partner
```

sam: Bindings show partner-svc@partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com and a legacy terraform account: tf-legacy@partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com. No direct internal accounts in that policy.

jake: Okay, partner-managed key is good — we probably never had plaintext. But the presence of our STAGING_* env var labels in logs suggests someone pushed an unredacted artifact to partner CI. We need to rotate any internal staging AWS creds and scan for unredacted dumps inside our CI history.

oncall: I've escalated to partner on-call. They acknowledged and are standing by to rewrap / rotate.

maria: Action items I propose: 
- A1: Run repo/CI search for STAGING_AWS_* env vars and leak candidates (maria)
- A2: Revoke staging AWS keys in our account and issue new temporary keys with constrained scope (lee)
- A3: Rotate any Vault KV entries that might have contained staging creds (sam)
- A4: Ask partner to rewrap or revoke ciphertext and confirm deletion from their storage (jake + partner)
- A5: Audit KMS unwrap logs (partner) and our forwarding logs (maria)

lee: I can rotate staging AWS keys now — will create limited IAM role for test service only. ETA 30m.

sam: For Vault, do we have a mapping from env var name -> secret path? If so I'll rotate and increment versions.
maria: mapping looks like: STAGING_AWS -> secret/staging/aws/creds. But that secret was last updated 4 months ago. I'll trigger an immediate rotation and set a short TTL.

jake: When rotating, prefer issuing ephemeral STS creds (AWS AssumeRole with external ID) so long-lived keys aren't used for staging. We should also add a leakage detection rule to CI to block artifacts containing :AKIA or common key prefixes.

security-bot: Reminder: update audit log retention flag when rotating. 

maria: I'm running a quick search in our artifact storage: 
```
# sample command
gsutil cat gs://partner-artifacts/2026-03-20/build-*/stdout | grep -E "STAGING_AWS|AKIA" -n || true
```

maria: Found two internal artifacts that referenced STAGING_AWS_*, one from deploy-staging-legacy and one from a thirdparty integration test. Saving hits to /tmp/leak-hits-1768009999.txt and sharing with eng-security.

lee: Lee -> I've revoked the old staging AWS keys and created role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/staging-temp. New creds (rotated) will be injected via Vault dynamic role.

sam: I'm rotating secret/staging/aws/creds in Vault now. Using vault lease manager to issue a short-lived credential: 
```
vault write auth/aws/role/staging-role auth_type=iam bound_iam_principal_arn=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/staging-temp ttl=1h
```

sam: Updated Vault entry and incremented version to v5. Notifying apps to pick up the new path.

jake: Partner responded: they didn't unwrap locally; their CI just stored the blob. They'll delete the artifacts and rotate their key if needed. They asked for a timestamp range of affected artifacts. Maria can you share list?

maria: Shared /tmp/leak-hits-1768009999.txt to eng-security drive and pinged partner with file.

lee: Also adding an RBAC block: removing any legacy terraform SA from partner workspace that had access to our callback endpoints. Sent PR to partner-admins.

oncall: Thanks — I'm updating the incident ticket with timeline, owners, and next steps. Could everyone ack their action? :thumbsup:

maria: ack

sam: ack — will keep Vault rotation on a short cadence for 24h and run smoke tests.

jake: ack — adding CI rule to block common key patterns. Deploying rule in ~1h.

lee: ack — I'll coordinate with infra to make staging use IAM-bound roles and external IDs.

security-bot: Incident update logged. Resolution target: rotate all affected internal credentials and confirm partner artifact deletion. Next update in 2h.

maria: final note — let's add an immediate CI pre-commit hook for scanning creds and a PR to our onboarding docs about never copying env files to partner repos. Small policy change but should cut future noise.

jake: agreed. I'll draft the CI rule and a short PR.

maria: thanks team. Closing thread here, moving detailed notes to INCIDENT-2026-1452 channel. 

security-bot: THREAD CLOSED (moved details to INC-2026-1452).
